principle_1_split_by_prompt.name: Split by prompt, not by record
principle_1_split_by_prompt.summary: Every model's row for one prompt lands on the same side of the train/test boundary, and whole out-of-distribution datasets go to test.
principle_1_split_by_prompt.tradeoff: Eliminates the leak that makes a per-prompt quality predictor look clairvoyant; costs training data and makes the test split harder than the train split on purpose.

principle_2_report_both_axes.name: Report quality and dollars side by side, never pre-scalarised
principle_2_report_both_axes.summary: The harness refuses to collapse quality and cost into one number; the weighting is a property of the policy under test, not of the scoreboard.
principle_2_report_both_axes.tradeoff: Honest and comparable; makes ranking policies a judgement call rather than a sort.

principle_3_bracket_with_references.name: Bracket every result between a random router, the single best model and an oracle
principle_3_bracket_with_references.summary: Three reference rows make an absolute number interpretable: below random is broken, above the best single model is real routing gain, the oracle is the ceiling.
principle_3_bracket_with_references.tradeoff: Turns any measured number into a position on a known interval; requires computing the oracle, which only an offline frozen matrix permits.

principle_4_freeze_the_dollars.name: Freeze measured dollars per record
principle_4_freeze_the_dollars.summary: Cost is measured once from real provider usage (preferring the provider's own reported cost over a list-price estimate) and then replayed, so a policy comparison is not confounded by price drift.
principle_4_freeze_the_dollars.tradeoff: Reproducible and cheap to re-run; the frozen rates absorb per-model verbosity and are not list prices.

principle_5_hard_budget_as_infeasibility.name: A hard budget is expressed as infeasibility, not as a penalty
principle_5_hard_budget_as_infeasibility.summary: An over-budget choice is scored as unusable rather than merely expensive, so the policy cannot buy its way past the cap.
principle_5_hard_budget_as_infeasibility.tradeoff: Makes the cap real; can leave a prompt with no feasible option at all, which the policy must then handle.
